refusal.present: No Principal intervention other than a legitimate `needs_ruling`.

recovery.present: Live variants of the corpus scenarios that need real agents: a reviewer-requested revision returned to the same session; a source-requiring task.

adversarial.notApplicable: Whole-loop orchestration on real tasks; adversarial inputs are §6.15 and §13 rows.

grader.detail: All binary: hidden tests on the final repository state, the ready-for-merge decision with every §16.10 condition, a trace predicate on handoffs, and the intervention record.

modules.decisionRule: §10: critical tasks — every trial of every critical task succeeds (pass^3 = 1 per task), designated before the run; remaining tasks — the *Principal* suite-level pass^3 floor with spend and wall time within the declared budget, no unadjudicated paired regression, non-inferiority from the milestone-3 paired pilot.

Recommended order: step 7, whole loop, rollback and cutover authorization.

modules.title: Backend selection and rollback (Engine gate 13)
modules.contract: The backend is selected and pinned per run when it starts and never changes for that run; neither backend resumes the other's state; rollback changes only the default for new runs, and each in-flight Engine run either continues on the Engine backend or is ended by the typed terminate-and-restart procedure.
modules.officialBasis: Vinaya product decision; LangGraph — Test (principle 12) for its L3 graph conformance: a fresh checkpointer per test, nodes alone, sections by partial execution.

positive.present: One new run started after the default is switched back to standalone is pinned to standalone.

negative.present: Each in-flight Engine run — in each pause kind, mid-Developer turn, mid-review, with an uncertain effect — continued on the Engine backend reaches the terminal state it reaches without rollback.

refusal.present: An attempt to resume an Engine run under the standalone backend is refused with a typed reason.

recovery.present: Each in-flight run terminated and restarted: cancelled, every prepared and uncertain effect reconciled by identity, restarted from the same prepared inputs with no effect duplicated or lost.

adversarial.notApplicable: §6.20 names no adversarial input; rollback is exercised against the program's own pause and effect states.

grader.detail: Code: the new run pinned to standalone; continued runs reach their unrolled terminal state; restarted runs start from the reconciled state; the cross-backend resume refused with a typed reason; the rehearsal record retained.

modules.decisionRule: Deterministic 100%; one live rehearsal at L6 before cutover, its record retained.
modules.migrationGate: §14: both backends execute its suites (backend-selection.l2@1, backend-selection.l3@1, backend-selection.l6@1); on its deterministic suites the Engine backend passes every mandatory case and every standalone failure is named by a registered expected defect, comparison evidence only; its live suites run the same tasks on both backends and meet their §10 rules on the Engine backend; its suites run in the regression floor or the live schedule on both backends until cutover and on the Engine backend afterwards; each of its §13 rows satisfies its declared cutover outcome. Recommended order: step 7, whole loop, rollback and cutover authorization.

modules.officialBasis: Claude Code — memory and CLAUDE.md, and Skills; Codex — Custom instructions with AGENTS.md, and Build skills.

positive.present: Loaded on first and resumed Developer sessions and on fresh reviewer sessions, both vendors.

negative.present: A missing, unreadable or shadowed instruction file is detected.

modules.title: Host dispatch readiness (sandbox)

positive.present: A ready host passes and dispatches.

negative.present: A sandbox that starts and then fails on its first command; agent instruction files absent from their vendor location.

refusal.present: A missing sandbox dependency refuses before any agent turn is counted.

recovery.notApplicable: Readiness only refuses; repairing the host is an Operator-remediation pause (§6.14).

adversarial.notApplicable: Readiness checks the host, not hostile input; confinement attacks are §6.15 cases.

modules.title: Operator role and capabilities (Engine §16.11; contracts §3)
modules.contract: The Operator's five run-control tools and the supporting pull-request read act only on the task they are scoped to, through the same run-control operations automation uses; every read leaves control state unchanged; a resume or cancel against stale, unavailable or already-terminal state is refused with a typed reason; the Operator never acts inside a round and never supplies a Principal ruling.
modules.officialBasis: Vinaya product decision; MCP — Tools, for discovery and error shape.

positive.present: Each capability on a live task; on realistic Operator requests the right capability is selected (L5).

negative.present: Another task's identity; an unauthenticated caller.

refusal.present: Resume of a run that is not paused, cancel of a terminal run, resume of an Operator-remediation pause whose preconditions do not yet hold.

recovery.present: Resume after the environment is repaired.

adversarial.present: A read used to mutate control state; a resume attempted as a substitute for a Principal ruling.

grader.detail: Code: control-state and audit assertions; a trace predicate on capability choice.

modules.decisionRule: 100% on every authority, scoping and refusal case, deterministic and live; capability selection on held-out Operator requests at ≥ 0.95 pass^3 (§10), with non-inferiority from the milestone-3 paired pilot.
modules.migrationGate: §14: both backends execute its suites (operator.l1@1, operator.l2@1, operator.l4@1, operator.l5@1); on its deterministic suites the Engine backend passes every mandatory case and every standalone failure is named by a registered expected defect, comparison evidence only; its live suites run the same tasks on both backends and meet their §10 rules on the Engine backend; its suites run in the regression floor or the live schedule on both backends until cutover and on the Engine backend afterwards; each of its §13 rows satisfies its declared cutover outcome. Recommended order: step 3, runtime mechanics.

modules.title: Cutover authorization evidence (Engine gate 17)
modules.contract: The default-backend change takes effect only on a valid Principal approval: authenticated, bound to the exact candidate and to the digest of the evidence for gates 1–16, fresh, with every gate 1–16 satisfied and every "pass or accepted" row of §13 passing or explicitly accepted.
modules.officialBasis: Vinaya product decision.

positive.present: A valid approval.

negative.present: Wrong actor, unauthenticated approval, approval bound to another candidate or evidence digest.

refusal.present: Any gate 1–16 unsatisfied; an unaccepted residual risk.

recovery.notApplicable: An approval is valid or it is not; a refused approval is replaced by a new one, not recovered.

adversarial.present: An approval replayed after new evidence or a newer candidate.

grader.detail: Code: approval validity and binding assertions.
